system.name: RamRyder
system.one_liner: a system that manages DIMM and CXL memory channels in software for elastic, isolated capacity and bandwidth allocation to VMs

components.name: Large VM
components.role: VM whose guest physical memory (GPM) is mapped across many channels for high bandwidth

components.name: Medium VM
components.role: VM mapped across a medium number of channels for medium bandwidth

components.name: Small VM
components.role: VM mapped across few channels for low bandwidth

components.name: GPM
components.role: guest physical memory region inside a VM that the hypervisor maps to channel devices

components.name: MEM
components.role: physical memory device (DIMM or CXL) attached to a channel and mapped into a VM's GPM

components.name: sNode
components.role: S-NUMA node aggregating cNodes from the same socket/zNUMA domain, exposed to the guest OS

components.name: cNode
components.role: C-NUMA node virtualizing the guest physical memory mapped to one memory channel

components.name: DIMM
components.role: statically allocated hardware memory device attached to a channel

components.name: CXL
components.role: CXL memory device attached to a channel

components.name: Channel
components.role: a memory channel; the unit RamRyder allocates and virtualizes

content.key_idea: RamRyder gives a VM as many memory channels as its target bandwidth requires (a), and exposes each channel to the guest OS as a cNode that is grouped by socket/zNUMA domain into a coarser sNode (b).
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) reads left-to-right across three VM sizes with increasing channel count for higher bandwidth; right panel (b) reads top-down from guest-visible sNode/cNode NUMA nodes to the physical DIMM/CXL channels below the Guest OS/hardware boundary.

summary: RamRyder allocates and virtualizes memory channels for VMs. Figure 7 has two panels. Panel (a), Channel Allocation, shows a Large, Medium and Small VM, each with a guest physical memory (GPM) region mapped by the hypervisor to a shrinking number of DIMM/CXL channels (MEM boxes), giving high, medium and low bandwidth respectively. Panel (b), Channel Abstraction, shows how each physical channel (DIMM or CXL) is virtualized as a C-NUMA node (cNode); cNodes from the same server socket or zNUMA domain are then grouped by the guest kernel into a coarser S-NUMA node (sNode) exposed above a dashed Guest-OS/hardware boundary. Both panels use flat cream and gray-blue fills to distinguish DIMM from CXL channels, rounded navy-outlined boxes, small sans-serif labels, and curly-brace groupings to show channels aggregating into higher-level abstractions.
summary_zh: 图7分两部分：(a)通道分配示大/中/小型VM按带宽需求映射到不同数量的DIMM/CXL通道；(b)通道抽象示每通道虚拟化为cNode，同插槽/zNUMA域内的cNode聚合为更高层sNode，虚线分隔客户OS与硬件。
